aspects.says: A lambda can't capture a basic for's counter, which the update changes; a variable declared in the body, or the enhanced for's variable, is new each pass and can be captured.
basis: section:A Lambda Can Capture the Enhanced for's Variable, Not the Basic for's Counter

aspects.says: A double counter accumulates rounding, so the number of passes can be one more or one fewer than the decimal values suggest; count with an int and compute the value from it.
basis: section:A Floating-Point Counter Changes the Number of Passes, So Count With an int

aspects.says: From 2^24 on, adjacent floats are 2 apart, so a float counter incremented by 1 stops moving and the loop never ends.
basis: section:A Floating-Point Counter Changes the Number of Passes, So Count With an int

aspects.says: The enhanced for copies each element into a new local variable, so assigning to that variable leaves the array or collection unchanged; writing back needs an index loop.
basis: section:The Enhanced for Copies Each Element Into Its Own Variable, So Assigning to It Changes Nothing

aspects.says: The enhanced for accepts an array or an Iterable, not a Stream, and throws NullPointerException before the first pass when the expression is null.
aspects.reason: a lookup of what compiles and what the header does with null; a graded test can't run code that doesn't compile, and the null case is a one-line fact the page states

aspects.says: With a primitive loop variable over a collection of wrappers, a null element throws NullPointerException as it is copied, before any check in the body runs.
basis: section:The Enhanced for Copies Each Element Into Its Own Variable, So Assigning to It Changes Nothing

aspects.says: A mutable holder used as the counter compiles, but every lambda reads it when it runs, so tasks run after the loop all see its final value.
basis: section:A Lambda Can Capture the Enhanced for's Variable, Not the Basic for's Counter

aspects.says: With < instead of <= on an inclusive bound, a last batch of a single element is never processed.
basis: section:A Loop Ends Only When Its Condition Turns False, and int Overflow Can Keep It True

aspects.says: A loop whose int counter must pass Integer.MAX_VALUE, or whose step overflows, never makes its condition false; a long counter ends it.
basis: section:A Loop Ends Only When Its Condition Turns False, and int Overflow Can Keep It True
